agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.mechanism: In Senegal's Ferlo, air under Acacia tortilis ranged between 29 °C and 36 °C against 26 °C and 42 °C outside, and access to cool zones under trees reduces livestock heat stress and raises animal productivity [ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_livestock_productivity_faosen24_22]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, maximum daily temperature fell by an average of 1–2.5 °C and minimum air humidity rose by up to 5%, with stronger differences on hotter and drier days [ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.conditionality: The Senegal units come from a review citing earlier studies and the Sahelian parkland figure is likewise a cited result; the temperature figures are canopy measurements, and the productivity gain is stated without a size [ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_livestock_productivity_faosen24_22, ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.mechanism: Parkland trees cool crops and livestock: midday air temperature under Faidherbia albida canopies on Ethiopian wheat farms was up to 6°C lower than in the open field, peaking at 29 °C under the canopy against 36 °C outside [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1]. In the same Ethiopian study, a crop model found that the lower temperature under F. albida shade raised simulated wheat yield when nitrogen was applied, but without applied N simulated yield was extremely small and did not respond to temperature [ev_crop_yield_sida18_3, ev_crop_yield_sida18_4]. In Senegal's Ferlo, air under Acacia tortilis ranged between 29 °C and 36 °C against 26 °C and 42 °C outside, and access to cool zones under trees reduces livestock heat stress and raises animal productivity [ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_livestock_productivity_faosen24_22]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, maximum daily temperature fell by an average of 1–2.5 °C and minimum air humidity rose by up to 5%, with stronger differences on hotter and drier days [ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.conditionality: The Ethiopian cooling was measured directly on farm; the other units are reviews citing earlier studies, and all report canopy temperature or animal comfort, entering as components of heat-stress impact [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_livestock_productivity_faosen24_22, ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2]. The yield link is modelled rather than measured, and the model's null without applied N is the no-benefit result that discounts the class: on unfertilised wheat the cooling did not carry through to simulated yield [ev_crop_yield_sida18_3, ev_crop_yield_sida18_4].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.mechanism: Faidherbia albida parkland trees on Ethiopian wheat farms lowered midday air temperature by up to 6°C against the open field: it peaked at 36 °C in the open and at 29 °C under the canopy, and exceeded 28 °C for about six hours a day in the open against less than two hours under the trees [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1]. A crop model in the same study found that this cooling raised simulated wheat yield when nitrogen was applied [ev_crop_yield_sida18_3].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.conditionality: Without applied N, simulated wheat yield was extremely small and did not respond to temperature, so the benefit depends on fertilisation; this modelled null is the no-benefit result that discounts the class [ev_crop_yield_sida18_4]. All units come from a single Ethiopian on-farm study in low-income rainfed cropping, within the LIC/LMIC target; the cooling was measured, the yield response modelled [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_3].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.mechanism: Faidherbia albida parkland trees on Ethiopian wheat farms lowered midday air temperature by up to 6°C, peaking at 29 °C under the canopy against 36 °C in the open field, and in Senegal's Ferlo air temperatures under Acacia tortilis ranged between 29 °C and 36 °C against 26 °C to 42 °C outside the cover [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, maximum daily temperature fell by an average of 1–2.5 °C and minimum air humidity rose by up to 5%, with stronger differences on hotter and drier days [ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__hea.conditionality: These are temperature measurements under tree canopies (the Ethiopian one measured on farm, the Senegalese and Sahelian ones cited from earlier studies), linked to heat stress through microclimate buffering rather than a measured heat-stress outcome [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2]. They come from low-income Ethiopia, lower-middle-income Senegal and the wider Sahel [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_6, ev_microclimate_buffering_bayala14_2].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__pro.mechanism: Millet yields are reported to double or triple under Faidherbia albida in Senegal, a cited meta-analysis reports mean yield increases of 150 per cent for maize and 73 per cent for sorghum under its canopy, and millet and groundnut yields were higher in plots with intensive FMNR [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_8, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_9, ev_crop_yield_seghieri19_14]. On paired on-farm plots in Ethiopia, wheat under Faidherbia albida crowns yielded 23-26% more grain than open-field wheat in the normal seasons of 2013 and 2014, and up to 85% more in 2015, an El Niño year in which both yields were low; available N close to the crowns was 35-55% larger than under sole wheat [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_1]. Shrubs on Sudano-Sahelian fields often raised millet and sorghum yields (−25 to + 120%), and soil nitrogen was higher beneath shrubs and Faidherbia albida canopies, used here as a component [ev_crop_yield_felix18_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_felix18_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_faosen24_2]. WOCAT practitioner ratings for FMNR in Kenya and assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso record higher crop and fodder production, the Kenyan compiler adding that well-managed FMNR land gives more and better-quality fodder than unmanaged land [ev_crop_yield_wocat_507_2019_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1358_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_507_2019_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1358_2017_fodder_production]. In Maradi, Niger, millet yields rose by 120 to 209 kg/ha where FMNR was older than 6 years, with smaller increases for younger FMNR, and FMNR is estimated to have raised yields by an average of 100 kg/ha over 5 million hectares [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3]. In Lempira, Honduras, the Quesungual system raised maize yields from 1.9 to 3.2 tonnes per hectare and bean yields from 0.8 to 2.0 tonnes per hectare, and its crops withstood the severe 1997 drought that caused losses for non-adopters [ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_2, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_3]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, tuber yield is improved (+0.40 to +1.67 t ha-1) and legumes are less affected than cereals, and tree fodder is crucial in the dry season and during drought [ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1, ev_forage_productivity_bayala14_1].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__pro.conditionality: Groundnut under Faidherbia albida behaved variably and groundnut and millet yields fell under Cordyla pinnata, so the effect depends on which trees are retained [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_10, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_11]. The pooled magnitude draws on two soil-nitrogen percentages and an FMNR crop-value figure from a self-evaluation brief that calls results elsewhere mixed, and the Ghana figure is a share of households reporting higher yield [ev_soil_nitrogen_faosen24_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_felix18_1, ev_crop_yield_wvfmnr19_4, ev_crop_yield_talensi21_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not yield measurements [ev_crop_yield_wocat_507_2019_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1358_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_507_2019_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1358_2017_fodder_production]. Cereals often lose: in Maradi, FMNR did not significantly increase grain yields, the income gain being attributed to crop diversification instead, and under parkland trees cereal grain yield ranged from a loss of 0.54 t ha-1 under Balanites aegyptiaca to a gain of 0.24 t ha-1 under F. albida, with reductions attributed to competition for light, nutrients and water [ev_crop_yield_haglund11_1, ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1]. The Niger yield figures are earlier estimates cited in a grey-literature review, and the Honduran yields are before-and-after case-study figures for a slash-and-mulch system [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1]. The Ethiopian drought-year gain stays separate from the normal-season gain; at the same site soil total N did not differ significantly under and outside the canopy at the end of the 2013 season despite the larger available N near the crowns, and the yield benefit of canopy cooling is modelled and appeared only with applied N [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_2, ev_crop_yield_sida18_3, ev_crop_yield_sida18_4].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__rur.mechanism: Senegalese households practising intensive FMNR gain on average 72.65 USD per season from selling non-timber products against 29.73 USD for others, the annual value of FMNR in Niger through soil fertility, firewood and fodder was calculated at US$56 per hectare, and FMNR project participants were 15 percent points more likely to report higher household income [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_economic_return_wvfmnr19_7, ev_household_income_wvfmnr19_5]. In Talensi, Ghana the share of households with sufficient diet diversity rose between the 2017 baseline and 2020 endline [ev_food_security_talensi21_3]. WOCAT practitioner ratings for FMNR in Kenya and assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso record higher farm income and food security, the Kenyan compiler crediting new income from wood, honey, medicinal and other non-wood products and more diversified livelihoods that reduce the risk of food insecurity [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1358_2017_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_507_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Both sheets also rate the long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive to very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. Across World Vision FMNR projects, participant households were nine percentage points more likely than non-participants to report a decrease in poverty in their communities, reported similarly by poorer and female-headed households [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. In Maradi, Niger, FMNR adoption increased gross annual household income by between 46 and 56 USD per capita compared with propensity-matched non-adopters, and the annual benefit-cost ratio of practising FMNR was estimated at between 2.5 and 3.0 [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_economic_return_haglund11_1]. In south-central Niger, sales of fuelwood and service wood from FMNR raise the income of all social categories, even the vulnerable and very vulnerable, and the net present value of FMNR at 10% over 20 years was €772 per hectare [ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__rur.conditionality: Several units are World Vision self-evaluations or figures cited in them; the social return on investment is a monetised social-value construct, and the Talensi diet result belongs to a bundled project rather than FMNR alone [ev_economic_return_wvfmnr19_8, ev_food_security_talensi21_3, ev_household_income_wvfmnr19_5]. Income and food security are proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_food_security_talensi21_3]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not household survey results, and like the other units they measure income or food security as proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The cost-benefit ratings are compiler judgements on a very-negative to very-positive scale, not measured returns [ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. The World Vision poverty result is a self-reported community perception, and the brief states FMNR cannot be fully separated from other project activities [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. In Maradi, FMNR did not appear to reduce the number of months of perceived food shortage [ev_food_security_haglund11_1]. The Maradi income and benefit-cost figures come from a matched survey comparison, while the fuelwood and net-present-value figures are cited in a grey-literature review [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__soi.mechanism: Across World Vision FMNR projects, participants were 10 percent points more likely than non-participants to report a reduction in erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_wvfmnr19_3]. WOCAT practitioner ratings add reduced soil loss and surface runoff under assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso, and less downstream siltation of ponds and water pans under FMNR in Kenya owing to less wind and water erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1358_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1358_2017_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation]. During Hurricane Mitch in October 1998, Honduran farmers practising the Quesungual system suffered less landslide damage than those using traditional slash-and-burn [ev_erosion_hazard_chaudhury11_1].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__soi.conditionality: The World Vision result is a reported perception from a self-evaluation in which the FMNR effect cannot be fully separated from other project activities [ev_erosion_hazard_wvfmnr19_3]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not erosion measurements, and the runoff and siltation ratings enter as components [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1358_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1358_2017_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation]. The Honduran landslide result is an earlier observation cited in a working paper, for a slash-and-mulch system under very intense rainfall [ev_erosion_hazard_chaudhury11_1].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__wat.mechanism: The Kenyan FMNR WOCAT sheet rates reduced downstream siltation, its compiler noting that less wind and water erosion reduces the siltation of ponds and water pans [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__wat.conditionality: The cell rests on a single compiler judgement from a technology sheet in lower-middle-income Kenya; siltation enters as a component of water-quality risk, and no unit measures water quality itself [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation].

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__wat.mechanism: Regenerated and retained trees on farmland compete with the crop for deeper soil water: under Faidherbia albida parkland in Ethiopia, soil moisture in the sub-soil was the least for wheat with tree, intermediate for sole tree and the highest for open field, while the authors observed no variation in topsoil moisture content between treatments [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_2]. That measured subsoil depletion is a harm to crop water supply for the adopter. WOCAT practitioner ratings point the other way, with improved water harvesting under assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso, and increased water availability under FMNR in Kenya, where the compiler credits greater water retention that raises groundwater levels [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1358_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__wat.conditionality: The direction is set by the measured Ethiopian study; the WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets rather than soil-moisture measurements and weigh little against it [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1358_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability]. The ratings and the measurement need not contradict: the ratings speak of water harvesting and groundwater, the measurement of subsoil water under a growing crop. The Ethiopian parkland trees were heavily pruned on farmers' fields; whether pruning or tree density changes the subsoil draw-down is not tested [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1]. The cited parkland tree-density result for groundwater recharge sits in the regeneration catchment water yield row.

agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__win.mechanism: Practitioner ratings on WOCAT sheets for regeneration practices in Burkina Faso and Kenya record reduced wind speed, the Kenyan compiler noting that FMNR trees serve as a windbreak protecting houses, greenhouses and crop fields against heavy winds [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1358_2017_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_507_2019_wind_velocity].
agroforestry__regeneration_farmland__win.conditionality: Both units are compiler judgements of wind speed on documented technology sheets for regeneration practices in low-income Burkina Faso and lower-middle-income Kenya, not measured storm or cyclone losses [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1358_2017_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_507_2019_wind_velocity].

agroforestry__rural_poverty.mechanism: Household income, economic return and food security are used as proxies for rural poverty [ev_household_income_castle21s_1, ev_economic_return_faosen24_15, ev_food_security_castle21s_1]. Positive results include Senegalese FMNR households earning more from non-timber products than non-adopters, calliandra fodder raising dairy farmers' net income in Kenya and Uganda, Vi Agroforestry advice raising Kenyan dietary diversity, and a windbreak hedge in Senegalese irrigated rice with an internal rate of return of 36 per cent [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_household_income_kiptot11_1, ev_food_security_castle21s_1, ev_economic_return_faosen24_15]. WOCAT practitioner ratings for FMNR in Kenya and assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso record higher farm income and food security, the Kenyan compiler crediting new income from wood, honey, medicinal and other non-wood products and more diversified livelihoods that reduce the risk of food insecurity [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1358_2017_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_507_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Both sheets also rate the long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive to very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. Across World Vision FMNR projects, participant households were nine percentage points more likely than non-participants to report a decrease in poverty in their communities, reported similarly by poorer and female-headed households [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. In Rwanda, tree products are a safety net: food-insecure farmers more often sold tree products for income than food-secure farmers, and tree density was positively associated with food security in some agroecologies [ev_household_income_ndoli21_1, ev_food_security_ndoli21_1]. In Nyando District, Kenya, agroforestry-project households typically used fewer detrimental coping strategies during hunger periods, sold fuel wood and timber to buy food during the drought, relied on tree fruit when floods washed crops away, and in Lower Nyando held more livestock wealth than control households [ev_food_security_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1, ev_household_income_thorlak12_2]. In Maradi, Niger, FMNR adoption increased gross annual household income by between 46 and 56 USD per capita compared with propensity-matched non-adopters, and the annual benefit-cost ratio of practising FMNR was estimated at between 2.5 and 3.0 [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_economic_return_haglund11_1]. In south-central Niger, sales of fuelwood and service wood from FMNR raise the income of all social categories, even the vulnerable and very vulnerable, and the net present value of FMNR at 10% over 20 years was €772 per hectare [ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1]. Fertilizer trees limit financial risk in drought years: where a crop fails, farmers using inorganic fertilizer lose the US$164 spent on the input, against US$90 for farmers who planted fertilizer trees [ev_economic_return_chaudhury11_1]. In a Mozambique carbon-forestry scheme promoting almost exclusively agroforestry, overall household income was generally increased [ev_household_income_lasco14_1]. In Colombia, intensive silvopasture had an operating benefit-cost ratio of 2.8 against 1.34 for a traditional system, and producer income from milk sales was 42.12% higher than under pasture monoculture owing to a higher carrying capacity [ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1]. A global systematic review of nature-based solutions for food security counts three cited population-survey studies finding positive results in food access where agroforestry was applied in southern Africa, Brazil and China over periods of up to 20 years [ev_food_security_nguy24n_1]. In the Nepal mid-hills, after a market-oriented agroforestry project of fodder-tree hedgerows and understorey cash crops, bundled with marketing support, training, seed subsidies and organic fertiliser, the share of participating households below the poverty line dropped from 48 % to 34 %, the share that was food sufficient rose from 52% to 69%, and the average farm-income figure rose from 37 to 48 percent, mainly from understorey crops, while off-farm income changed by -9% [ev_rural_poverty_pandit19_1, ev_food_security_pandit19_1, ev_household_income_pandit19_1]. In southern Malawi, under higher fertiliser prices the value-cost ratio of a Tephrosia vogelii relay intercrop with maize stayed above 4.0, which the authors call a profitable scenario, while the higher prices pulled monoculture maize down to 2.5 or less [ev_economic_return_snapp10_1]. In shaded coffee and cocoa, a meta-analysis found the average net return of shaded systems significantly higher by 23% than conventional systems [ev_economic_return_jezeer17_1], a case cited second-hand found a coffee price crash cut sun-coffee net revenue far more than that of extensive agroforestry [ev_economic_return_jezeer17_3], and a farm model for Costa Rica and Guatemala found smaller losses for high-shade systems under a 50% coffee price fall [ev_economic_return_lalani24_2].
agroforestry__rural_poverty.conditionality: Results are mixed: a systematic review's pooled income effect is small and not statistically significant, crop–fruit tree intercropping in China lowered gross household income, silvopasture income lags traditional pasture in the first years, and Regreening Africa found average tree-product income unchanged [ev_household_income_castle21s_1, ev_household_income_castle21s_2, ev_economic_return_diasf08_1, ev_household_income_rgaf23_6]. Several positive units are self-evaluations, bundled-project results or a modelled business case, and the proxies measure income or returns rather than poverty itself [ev_household_income_wvfmnr19_5, ev_food_security_talensi21_3, ev_household_income_cmscr20_6]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not household survey results, and like the other units they measure income or food security as proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The cost-benefit ratings are compiler judgements on a very-negative to very-positive scale, not measured returns [ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. The Colombian sustainable-ranching completion report found no measured poverty reduction at closing, because many silvopastoral systems were still in their establishment phase and project effects could not be separated from drought and other climatic events [ev_rural_poverty_cmscr20_9]. The World Vision poverty result is a self-reported community perception from participants [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. The Rwandan effect varied by agroecology: more trees went with higher food security in Congo Nile but lower food security in the Buberuka Highlands [ev_food_security_ndoli21_2]. The Lower Nyando livestock-wealth difference, used by the authors as an income surrogate, was not significant at conventional levels, and the timber-sales and flood-fruit findings are farmer-reported [ev_household_income_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1]. In Maradi, FMNR did not appear to reduce the number of months of perceived food shortage [ev_food_security_haglund11_1]. The Maradi income and benefit-cost figures come from a matched survey comparison, while the fuelwood and net-present-value figures are cited in a grey-literature review [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1]. The Zambian loss comparison and Mozambique result are earlier findings cited in a working paper and a review [ev_economic_return_chaudhury11_1, ev_household_income_lasco14_1]. The Colombian ratio and milk-income figures are earlier studies cited in a Spanish-language systematic review and a CATIE edited volume [ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1]. The food-access vote count comes from a low-tier systematic review that included only studies showing improvement in at least one food-security dimension, so its positive count is guaranteed by its inclusion rule and says nothing about studies that found no benefit; of its three cited studies, one is a life-cycle assessment rather than a population survey and another is not clearly agroforestry [ev_food_security_nguy24n_1]. The Nepal results come from a bundled project and are not credited in full to the trees: they are a before-and-after recall survey of participating households with no control group, and the share of the bundle due to agroforestry is not stated [ev_rural_poverty_pandit19_1, ev_food_security_pandit19_1, ev_household_income_pandit19_1]. The Malawian value-cost ratio is a fertiliser-price scenario on on-farm trial data, not measured household income [ev_economic_return_snapp10_1]. The shaded coffee and cocoa evidence also pulls both ways: in Guayas, Ecuador, technified cacao monoculture earned a higher net margin per hectare than organic or traditional cacao agroforestry [ev_economic_return_perezneira16_1, ev_economic_return_perezneira16_2], a pan-tropical cocoa meta-analysis found higher total system production not reflected in higher revenues or net present values [ev_economic_return_niether20_1, ev_household_income_niether20_1], and after Hurricane Stan coffee management had no effect on economic losses in Mexico [ev_economic_return_philpott08_1]; these units are crop-specific, and the price-fall result is modelled [ev_economic_return_lalani24_2].

agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.mechanism: In Senegal's southern-centre groundnut basin, households practising intensive FMNR earned on average 72.65 USD per season from selling non-timber products against 29.73 USD for other households, and 3 % of adopters against 14 % of non-adopters did not meet their annual food needs for more than 4 months (0 % against 4% in the northern-centre basin) [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_food_security_seghieri19_13]. In southern Malawi, under higher fertiliser prices the value-cost ratio of a Tephrosia vogelii relay intercrop with maize stayed above 4.0, which the authors call a profitable scenario, while the higher prices pulled monoculture maize down to 2.5 or less [ev_economic_return_snapp10_1].
agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.conditionality: Income, food sufficiency and returns stand in for poverty here rather than measuring it. The Senegal figures are adopter versus non-adopter survey comparisons with no stated significance test, taken from an English abstract inside a French volume, and the Malawian ratio is a fertiliser-price scenario on on-farm trial data rather than measured household income [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_food_security_seghieri19_13, ev_economic_return_snapp10_1]. The FMNR and Tephrosia results come from different sub-practices, regeneration-based farmland in Senegal and a planted relay intercrop in Malawi, which agree in direction only.

agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.mechanism: In Rwanda, tree products are a safety net: food-insecure farmers more often sold tree products for income than food-secure farmers, and tree density was positively associated with food security in some agroecologies [ev_household_income_ndoli21_1, ev_food_security_ndoli21_1]. In Nyando District, Kenya, agroforestry-project households typically used fewer detrimental coping strategies during hunger periods, sold fuel wood and timber to buy food during the drought, relied on tree fruit when floods washed crops away, and in Lower Nyando held more livestock wealth than control households [ev_food_security_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1, ev_household_income_thorlak12_2].
agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.conditionality: The Rwandan effect varied by agroecology: more trees went with higher food security in Congo Nile but lower food security in the Buberuka Highlands [ev_food_security_ndoli21_2]. The Lower Nyando livestock-wealth difference, used by the authors as an income surrogate, was not significant at conventional levels, and the timber-sales and flood-fruit findings are farmer-reported [ev_household_income_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1]. Household income, wealth and food security are used here as proxies for rural poverty, and the Rwandan units are cross-sectional associations rather than a comparison during a shock [ev_household_income_ndoli21_1, ev_food_security_ndoli21_1, ev_household_income_thorlak12_2].

agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.mechanism: Returns in tree-perennial agroforestry have been reported both above and below the alternative. In Bolivia the return on labour over the years was almost twice as high in agroforestry systems as in monocultures [ev_economic_return_dsantos23_7]. In a Brazilian system at Tomé-Açu, the rice component showed negative economic performance and black pepper was unprofitable in low-price cycles [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_6].
agroforestry__rural_poverty__farming_sys.conditionality: The two units measure different things: the Bolivian gain is a whole-system return per day of labour against monoculture, while the Brazilian loss is the performance of single components, which the authors say need adjustment in production, technology or management, and which depends on price cycles [ev_economic_return_dsantos23_7, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_6]. Component choice and exposure to price swings are therefore what a project would need to check. Both units are reviews citing earlier studies with no effect sizes and measure returns as a proxy, not poverty; they come from Bolivia (lower-middle income) and Brazil (upper-middle) [ev_economic_return_dsantos23_7, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_6].

agroforestry__rural_poverty__income_grou.mechanism: Agroforestry adds income and food through tree products and yields: FMNR in Niger is valued at US$56 per hectare a year in soil fertility, firewood, fodder and other products, FMNR-adopting households in Senegal earn 72.65 USD per season from non-timber products against 29.73 USD for others, and calliandra fodder raises farmers' net income in Kenya and Uganda by about US$ 101–122 a year by replacing dairy meal [ev_economic_return_wvfmnr19_7, ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_household_income_kiptot11_1]. Food-security gains include a dietary diversity score raised by 1.22 under Vi Agroforestry advice in Kenya, food crop value raised by 35% by fertilizer trees in Malawi, fewer months of food shortage among FMNR participants, and diet diversity rising with use of tree products [ev_food_security_castle21s_1, ev_t6_foodsec_ferttree_castle21_8, ev_food_security_wvfmnr19_9, ev_food_security_rgaf23_10]. A systematic review concludes that incomes improved through higher yields, payments for ecosystem services or higher prices from eco-certification [ev_t6_income_pathway_castle21_5].
agroforestry__rural_poverty__income_grou.conditionality: The pooled income effect is small and not significant (0.12 SMD, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.30), the meta-analysis ratios for revenue, profit and benefit-cost are not significant, and several units are null: tree-product income per household stayed at USD 82 PPP, food-insecurity scores barely changed, income change was not expected within the programme period, and improved fallows did not translate into household welfare on small farms [ev_household_income_castle21s_1, ev_economic_return_steward23wp_1, ev_economic_return_steward23wp_2, ev_economic_return_steward23wp_3, ev_household_income_rgaf23_6, ev_food_security_rgaf23_9, ev_household_income_crs23_5, ev_household_income_place05_2]. One unit points the other way: in Uganda, FMNR participants, who were often the poorer households, were less likely to report income gains [ev_household_income_wvfmnr19_6]. All evidence is from LIC/LMIC settings, but most units measure proxies for poverty (income, returns, food security) rather than poverty itself, and some results are bundled project outcomes or modelled scenarios, such as the Talensi diet and hungry-month changes and a Nigerian climate model [ev_economic_return_wvfmnr19_7, ev_food_security_castle21s_1, ev_food_security_talensi21_3, ev_food_security_talensi21_4, ev_household_income_watts22_14].

agroforestry__rural_poverty__income_grou.mechanism: Household income and economic returns stand in for poverty in this evidence, and they move in both directions. Gains: an integrative review of Brazilian family-farm agroforestry viability studies found all indices positive, with internal rates of return always above 7% and benefit-cost ratios above 1, most between 1.20 and 2.50 and some above 3.00; individual systems in Pará reached a benefit-cost ratio of 2.5 and an internal rate of return of 15%, or cleared a 10% hurdle rate [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_1, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_2, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_7, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_8]. In Colombia, silvopasture raised income through better animal nutrition, productivity and fertility and higher carrying capacity: a Bank-commissioned business case estimates up to US$523/ha more annual income with production costs US$127/ha lower, intensive silvopasture had an operating benefit-cost ratio of 2.8 against 1.34, milk-sale income was 42.12% higher than under pasture monoculture, and Caquetá farms in silvopastoral projects saw higher income from animal sales [ev_household_income_cmscr20_6, ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1, ev_household_income_bur24_1]. A Brazilian review also cites potential to raise profitability in municipalities prone to climate variation [ev_economic_return_ribeiro22_2]. Losses: crop–fruit tree intercropping in Xinjiang, China lowered gross household income (−0.29 SMD) [ev_household_income_castle21s_2]; silvopasture income lags traditional pasture in the first years after establishment [ev_economic_return_diasf08_1]; an organic agroforestry system in Paraná collapsed from the seventh year through lack of long-term management and planning, the rice component at Tomé-Açu lost money and black pepper did so in low-price cycles, and a multistrata coconut, lemon, passionfruit, cowpea and cassava system gave the lowest return of those assessed [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_5, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_6, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_9]. For Indonesian social-forestry permits, profitability was no better for permit holders than for households without one [ev_economic_return_castle21s_4].
agroforestry__rural_poverty__income_grou.conditionality: What separates the sides, where the evidence says: time since establishment, since silvopasture income lags in the early years and the Colombian completion report found no measured poverty reduction at closing because many systems were still being established and effects could not be separated from drought [ev_economic_return_diasf08_1, ev_rural_poverty_cmscr20_9]; long-term management and planning, the stated cause of the Paraná collapse [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_5]; the choice of components and their prices, with rice and black pepper losing and one multistrata mix earning least [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_6, ev_economic_return_ferraz24_9]; and system type, with the Colombian silvopasture gains set against the Xinjiang crop–fruit tree intercropping loss [ev_household_income_castle21s_2]. For a Task Team Leader the practical points are to plan for an establishment-period income gap and to vet component choice and long-term management. On evidence quality, the gain side leans on grey-literature Brazilian viability studies, earlier results cited in reviews, a modelled business case for the US$523/ha figure, and a brief with no effect size [ev_economic_return_ferraz24_1, ev_household_income_cmscr20_6, ev_household_income_bur24_1, ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1]; the Xinjiang loss is a quantified estimate from a systematic review, while the other losses are narrative case reports. All units measure income or returns rather than poverty itself.

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.mechanism: In cabruca cocoa agroforests in southern Bahia, Brazil, the El Niño drought of 2015 and 2016 killed 15% of cocoa trees against under 1% normally and 7% of the 317 woody shade trees, with no shade-tree species particularly affected; potential yield fell from 242 to 26 kg/ha, an 89% reduction, and was still 83% lower nine months after the drought ended [ev_establishment_survival_gateau18_1, ev_establishment_survival_gateau18_2, ev_crop_yield_gateau18_1]. A systematic review reads the same study as showing drought could increase mortality of cacao trees and their shade trees, implying tree shading may not be effective against drought [ev_tree_canopy_cover_watts22_5]. In Ghana, leguminous shade trees competed with the crop for soil water during severe drought, enhancing crop mortality compared with full sun [ev_tree_canopy_cover_ipccar6ch5_3].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.conditionality: Most of the weight is one observational study of one drought event in Bahia, read directly and second-hand through the review [ev_crop_yield_gateau18_1, ev_tree_canopy_cover_watts22_5]; it has no unshaded comparator, so it shows the damage to the shaded system, not that shade caused it. The Ghana shade-competition finding is the IPCC chapter's second-hand reading; the chapter writes coffee but the cited study is on cocoa [ev_tree_canopy_cover_ipccar6ch5_3]. Cocoa units are crop-specific and enter under the shaded-perennial crop-scope ruling. Brazil is upper-middle income and Ghana lower-middle income, adjacent to the LIC/LMIC target [ev_establishment_survival_gateau18_1, ev_tree_canopy_cover_ipccar6ch5_3].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.mechanism: A tropics review, citing earlier studies, reports that flooding increases tree mortality in cacao agroforests, with older systems potentially more vulnerable [ev_tree_canopy_cover_watts22_6].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.conditionality: The two units point different ways: a coconut review from Kerala, India, reports second-hand that the coconut palm withstands typhoons and flooding [ev_flood_hazard_kumar22_2], while the cacao mortality finding is the least robust grade in the review's own scheme [ev_tree_canopy_cover_watts22_6]. Both are second-hand readings and crop-specific, entering under the shaded-perennial crop-scope ruling; neither measures how much damage a flood does. India is lower-middle income [ev_flood_hazard_kumar22_2].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.mechanism: In shaded coffee in Soconusco, Chiapas, Mexico, a field study found minimal vegetation damage as a result of the hurricane, and no small landslides within the study plots [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_philpott08_7]. A coconut review from Kerala, India, reports, citing earlier work, that the coconut palm can withstand natural calamities like typhoons and flooding [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_kumar22_1].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__asset_th.conditionality: The measured finding comes from a single hurricane whose winds the unit records as mild, so it does not show shaded perennials withstand a severe cyclone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_philpott08_7]. The coconut statement is a second-hand review claim about the palm itself, not a measurement [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_kumar22_1]. Both are crop-specific and enter under the shaded-perennial crop-scope ruling. Mexico is upper-middle income and India lower-middle income, adjacent to the LIC/LMIC target [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_philpott08_7, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_kumar22_1].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__biodiver.mechanism: Shade trees over coffee and cocoa hold species that sun plantations lose. A meta-analysis of cocoa found a significantly higher number of animal species in agroforestry systems than in cocoa monocultures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_niether20_1]. A review of shaded coffee and cocoa reports, from a meta-analysis of 74 studies, a stronger decline in total species richness from agroforestry to plantations (−46%) than from forest to agroforestry (−11%), and, from another study, bird diversity between 120 and 306% higher in three shaded coffee systems [ev_biodiversity_outcome_jezeer17_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_jezeer17_2]. In Nicaraguan coffee, most certification schemes had positive impacts on a tree diversity index used as a proxy for habitat quality [ev_biodiversity_outcome_castle21s_1].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__biodiver.conditionality: The harm finding is a yield trade-off in Cameroonian cocoa: yields above 1 t/ha did not seem attainable with more than 10 associated species, while about 750 kg/ha was possible with up to 20-23 species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seghieri19_7]. Scheme design matters: C.A.F.E. Practices was the only Nicaraguan certification scheme with a negative impact on tree diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_castle21s_1]. The review figures and the Nicaraguan result are second-hand readings, and the review notes the shaded coffee systems had an overall decline in yield [ev_biodiversity_outcome_jezeer17_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_castle21s_1]. The richness drop from forest to agroforestry (−11%) marks that shaded systems hold less than forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_jezeer17_1]. All units are crop-specific and enter under the shaded-perennial crop-scope ruling; the cocoa meta-analysis draws mainly on lower-middle-income countries [ev_biodiversity_outcome_niether20_1].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__carbon_s.mechanism: Shade trees over coffee, cocoa and coconut add biomass and soil carbon over the crop grown alone. Total biomass carbon in cocoa agroforestry, including cocoa and shade trees, is on average 2.5 times higher than in monoculture [ev_carbon_sequestration_niether20_1]. In Costa Rican coffee agroforestry, an eight-year eddy-covariance carbon balance gave a mean storage of 3.6 t C/ha/yr, and shaded coffee plots held 29,8 Mg ha-1 more above-ground biomass carbon than full-sun plantations [ev_carbon_sequestration_seghieri19_5, ev_carbon_sequestration_villa20_6]. East African perennial tree-crop systems hold 29.9 Mg C ha−1 of above-ground carbon, and modelled Ethiopian enset-coffee and tree-coffee systems translate to biomass carbon of 139.5 and 153.4 Mg/ha [ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_4, ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_6]. A coconut review reports carbon storage by coconut palms in mixed stands is clearly greater than in sole stands, especially when the mix involves trees, and higher soil carbon sequestration in mixed-species systems [ev_carbon_sequestration_kumar22_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_kumar22_1]; a coffee review reports soil organic matter improved by 20–35% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_patil25_5].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__carbon_s.conditionality: Most units do not state a size, which caps the class. The soil side is mixed: the cocoa meta-analysis found no significant differences in soil chemical properties between agroforestry and monoculture [ev_soil_organic_carbon_niether20_1], and certified shade coffee in Nicaragua had positive but not statistically significant impacts on above-ground carbon stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_castle21s_1]. The coconut, coffee-soil and Nicaraguan units are second-hand readings, the Ethiopian figures are cited model outputs, and the East African and Ethiopian figures are stocks, not annual rates [ev_carbon_sequestration_kumar22_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_patil25_5, ev_carbon_sequestration_castle21s_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_6]. The Costa Rican coffee units are from a high-income country [ev_carbon_sequestration_seghieri19_5, ev_carbon_sequestration_villa20_6]. Crop-specific units enter under the shaded-perennial crop-scope ruling; the low- and lower-middle-income fit rests on the cocoa meta-analysis, the East African review, Nicaragua and India [ev_carbon_sequestration_niether20_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_4, ev_carbon_sequestration_kumar22_1].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__cost_red.mechanism: A pan-tropical meta-analysis of cocoa agroforestry against full-sun cocoa monocultures found that the higher total system production of agroforestry is not reflected in revenues, net present values or production costs: costs did not differ significantly between the systems [ev_project_cost_niether20_1].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__cost_red.conditionality: This is a single meta-analysis, so the cell has no second independent source to test agreement against, and its finding is a non-significant difference rather than a saving [ev_project_cost_niether20_1]. The evidence is crop-specific to cocoa (shaded perennial systems), drawn mostly from lower-middle-income producing countries, and the costs are recurrent production costs (labour, inputs), not establishment costs [ev_project_cost_niether20_1].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__drought_.mechanism: Under drought, shade over cocoa and coffee has been found to protect the crop, to compete with it for water, and to make no difference. On the protective side, in Ethiopia's Yayu coffee forest the yield model for the climate-shock years found leguminous shade strongly raised coffee shrub yields at high canopy openness [ev_crop_yield_morel24_1]; a review cites a 41% cut in evapotranspiration loss under coffee shade trees in the hot, dry season (Lin 2006) [ev_soil_water_retention_dobhal24_8]; and another cites low water stress in cacao grown with Gliricidia (Schwendenmann et al. 2010; Köhler et al. 2010) [ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_11]. On the competing side, reviews cite that under warmer, water-limited conditions competition between trees and cacao for scarce soil water can reduce soil moisture and cacao yields below those of open-sun farms (Blaser et al. 2018), that drought caused greater water loss in cacao agroforests than in open-sun cacao because trees and cacao both transpire (Abdulai et al. 2018), and that intercropping may compete for soil moisture during drought [ev_crop_yield_watts22_8, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_9, ev_soil_water_retention_patil25_8]. Between them sit no-effect findings: in a Ghana rainwater-suppression experiment the shade-by-drought interaction on yield was not significant, so shade did not prevent the drought-induced yield decline and the better performance of cocoa under shade only partly compensated for it [ev_crop_yield_mensah23_2]; the Ethiopian study did not directly observe benefits of diverse shade in the extreme climate shocks [ev_crop_yield_morel24_2]; and across cabruca cocoa farms in southern Bahia, Brazil, drought yield loss was unrelated to shade-tree ground cover [ev_crop_yield_gateau18_2].
agroforestry__shaded_perennial__drought_.conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates the sides, as far as the evidence says, is twofold. First, better crop performance under shade is not the same as protection from drought: the Ghana experiment found the effects of shade and rainwater suppression additive, so the drought loss itself was not buffered [ev_crop_yield_mensah23_2]. Second, whether the shade trees draw on the same scarce soil water as the crop: the losses are attributed to that competition and to combined tree and crop transpiration, while the gains come with a named companion tree (Gliricidia) or a shade-management setting (canopy openness) [ev_crop_yield_watts22_8, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_9, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_11, ev_crop_yield_morel24_1]. Shade-tree species, density and canopy management are therefore the design questions. All units are crop-specific (cocoa or coffee) and enter because shaded perennial-crop systems are judged on their host crop. The review units are second-hand readings of earlier studies, and only the evapotranspiration figure carries a size [ev_soil_water_retention_dobhal24_8, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_11, ev_crop_yield_watts22_8, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_9, ev_soil_water_retention_patil25_8]. The field units are from upper-middle-income Brazil, low-income Ethiopia and lower-middle-income Ghana; the review units record no country [ev_crop_yield_gateau18_2, ev_crop_yield_morel24_1, ev_crop_yield_mensah23_2].

agroforestry__shaded_perennial__drought_.conditionality: What separates the sides, as far as the evidence says, is twofold. First, a higher yield under shade is not the same as protection from drought: the Ghana experiment found the overall better performance of cocoa under shade can only partly compensate for the reduced yield during drought episodes [ev_crop_yield_mensah23_2]. Second, whether the shade trees draw on the same scarce soil water as the crop: the losses are attributed to that competition and to combined tree and crop transpiration, while the gains come with a named companion tree (Gliricidia) or a shade-management setting (canopy openness) [ev_crop_yield_watts22_8, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_9, ev_soil_water_retention_watts22_11, ev_crop_yield_morel24_1].
